leftEvidence.title: Israel crosses on dry ground as the sea divides and returns

points.label: Water and ground
points.left: The sea is driven back and Israel walks on dry ground.
points.right: Joshua recalls the Jordan drying before the people and compares it to the Red Sea.

points.label: Who makes the comparison
points.left: The Exodus Scene narrates the crossing and its immediate result.
points.right: Joshua explains the stones and tells a later generation how to speak about both crossings.

points.label: Stated audience
points.left: Israel sees what happened to the Egyptians and responds to the LORD and Moses.
points.right: The memorial is directed toward the peoples of the earth and Israel’s continuing fear of the LORD.

payload.posture: Keep the two crossings distinct while inspecting the comparison made inside Joshua.

rightEvidence.title: The dried Jordan is explicitly placed beside the dried Red Sea

payload.tension: Keep the two crossings distinct while inspecting the comparison made inside Joshua.
payload.title: Sea crossed / sea remembered at the Jordan
